column1: # 🔴 THE MECHANISM, and it is why NO licence-path ladder can ever settle this repository:
#    Twenty's own LICENSE says which files are commercial by naming A COMMENT IN THE SOURCE —
#    "/* @license Enterprise */" at the top of the file. A per-file grant selected by a CODE COMMENT
#    is invisible to every probe this KB owns, all of which read PATHS.
# 🟡 p220 wrote the rule "the unit of a licence is the FILE". Twenty is the first first-hand payload on
#    these shelves where the unit is the file AND the discriminator is not a file at all.
# 🟢 WHAT A STUDIO CAN ACTUALLY TAKE: twenty-ui and twenty-shared, MIT, verified at the package root.
#    NOT the server. The usable grant is a SUBTREE, and "AGPL, avoid" would have thrown it away.
# 🟡 A SECOND, SMALLER FINDING, on OpenEduCat: its LICENSE promises "the text of the GPL is included at
#    the bottom as well". The payload is 8241 B and ends on LGPLv3's own final clause. The GPLv3 text it
#    promises is NOT in the file — and LGPLv3 is DEFINED as additional permissions on top of the GPL.
